facts.fact: A study of 14,000 local business locations, cited by Adwave, found that businesses using centralized tools to sync listings saw a 28% jump in 'Discovery' search views within 90 days.
facts.quote: A study of **14,000** local business locations found that businesses using centralized tools to sync their listings saw a **28%** jump in 'Discovery' search views in just **90** days.

facts.fact: Adwave states that 46% of all Google searches have local intent, without citing a source.
facts.quote: When you consider that **46% of all Google searches have local intent**

facts.fact: Adwave says businesses with 10 or more locations are likely eligible for Google's bulk verification of Google Business Profile locations.
facts.quote: Fortunately, if you have **10 or more locations**, you're likely eligible for **bulk verification**.

facts.fact: The guide recommends writing a unique 750-character description for every individual Google Business Profile location.
facts.quote: take the time to write a unique, 750-character description for every single location that highlights what makes it special.

facts.fact: Per the vendor's own statement citing unspecified research, profiles with 10 or more images can easily double their engagement.
facts.quote: We've seen from research that profiles with **10 or more images** can easily double their engagement.

facts.fact: The vendor's policy is that businesses should respond to every single Google review.
facts.quote: it should be company policy to **respond to every single one**.

facts.fact: Google does not allow P.O. boxes or virtual offices as a business address and requires a real physical address where the team is present during business hours.
facts.quote: **Never use P.O. boxes or virtual offices.** Google demands a real, physical address where your team is present during business hours.

facts.fact: Service-area businesses should clearly define their service area and hide their physical address from public view on Google Business Profiles.
facts.quote: you must clearly define your service area and then hide your physical address from the public view.

facts.fact: The page predicts that by 2026 the most successful multi-location strategies will be those that master spam prevention and adapt to policy updates.
facts.quote: The algorithm is doubling down on spam removal, review quality, and accurate business categories.

facts.fact: The page advises reserving Google Business Profile's Owner role for one or two key people at the corporate level.
facts.quote: Reserve this for one or two key people at the corporate level.

facts.fact: Per the page, a Google Business Profile Manager role can handle day-to-day tasks such as replying to reviews and creating posts, but cannot add users or delete the profile.
facts.quote: Can handle most day-to-day tasks like responding to reviews or creating posts, but can't add users or delete the profile.

facts.fact: The page says that businesses with 10 or more locations should use bulk verification for Google Business Profile listings rather than waiting for postcards.
facts.quote: If you have **10 or more locations**, forget about waiting for postcards in the mail.

facts.fact: The page says the Site Manager role is suited to an individual store manager who needs to update hours or reply to reviews for their own location.
facts.quote: This role is ideal for an individual store manager who just needs to update hours or reply to reviews for their specific location.

facts.fact: The page states that the Google Business Profile Performance report can be filtered to a single location, a custom group, or the entire business.
facts.quote: you can easily filter the view to see data for one specific location, a custom group (like all your "Texas Stores"), or your entire business.
